_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Finding the cheapest places to go

description: Use when the traveler wants the cheapest place to fly from somewhere, or ideas for where to go, instead of a destination they already chose: "the cheapest flight from Warsaw, anywhere", "where can I go cheaply", "the cheapest city in Brazil". Returns destinations cheapest first with the airline, stops and a search_url: priced on the traveler's dates when you give depart_date (and return_date for a round trip), else each on its own cheapest dates in the coming months.

abroad.description: Only places outside the origin's country, when the traveler says out of the country, abroad or international.
abroad.title: Abroad

country_or_region.description: Only destinations in this country or region, as the traveler said it.
country_or_region.title: Country Or Region

depart_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD: price every place on this day (the traveler's own). Empty: each on its own cheapest dates.
depart_date.title: Depart Date

max_price_usd.description: Only fares at or under this total, in US dollars.
max_price_usd.title: Max Price Usd

origin.description: A 3-letter airport code (JFK), or a city code that searches every airport in the city (SlickTrip's 4-letter codes: NYCA New York, LOND London, ROME Rome, TYOA Tokyo). Up to 3 places joined with _ search them together (JFK_EWR). A place name works when one place clearly matches; otherwise the result is an unknown_place error listing suggestions. When the traveler names a city rather than an airport, send the city (its name or code), not one of its airports: one airport can miss the cheapest or the only flights. Unsure of the code: call find_places.
origin.title: Origin

return_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, with depart_date, for a round trip.
return_date.title: Return Date

travelers.description: Travelers who need a seat (adults and children). Fares are quoted for all of them together; one booking holds up to 9 (a larger group gets a suggested split). A baby under 2 on a lap is not a seat and is not counted here.
travelers.title: Travelers

user_request.description: Optional, and it works in the traveler's favor. Quote the traveler's latest message about this trip exactly as they wrote it, in their wording, language and spelling, not a summary. SlickTrip runs its own travel parser on these words: when a search fails or comes back empty, it compares what the traveler said with the arguments sent and returns a corrected search, so you can fix it without asking them again. It has caught Cancun sent as MEX instead of CUN, and travelers dropped from the party. A summary loses exactly the details it checks. If the message only answers a question ("yes, the 20th"), quote the message where they asked for the trip. Send the same quote on every call for this request. Leave out anything not about the trip, and never include names, contact details, or payment or ID information. The words also help SlickTrip improve its search.
examples: we're 6 friends from madrid, want somewhere cheap and fun in europe dec 20-24, morning flights pls
necesito llevar a mi mamá de Calgary a Kolkata a fines de octubre, no puede hacer escala en Estados Unidos
user_request.title: User Request

name: explore_destinations

code.description: On an error: a machine-readable kind, e.g. unknown_place

destinations.description: city, country, airport, price_usd (total), per_traveler_usd, depart_date, return_date, airline, stops, duration_minutes, search_url

message.description: What went wrong, when status is error

note.description: How to read and use the list

places_assumed.description: Place names this call resolved on its own, e.g. 'Portland = Portland, OR (PDX)'; tell the traveler

search.description: origin, trip_type, travelers, cabin, nonstop, country_or_region, max_price_usd

suggestions.description: On unknown_place: places to offer the traveler, each with code, name, kind (airport, all airports in the city, nearby airport), city, country

title: Cheapest places to go
